title: Distributed Sliding-Window Rate Limiting Gateway in Go & Redis
problem: Public APIs and multi-tenant cloud platforms frequently experience abusive traffic spikes, credential stuffing attacks, and noisy-neighbor service degradation. Simple in-memory rate limiting fails across horizontally autoscaled service instances because local nodes lack shared global state. This project builds a distributed, low-latency API rate limiting proxy gateway in Go coordinated via Redis. The system implements atomic sliding-window counter and token bucket algorithms via Lua scripts to eliminate race conditions, supports multi-tier tenant quotas, returns standard RFC 6585 rate limiting headers, and provides an in-memory circuit breaker that gracefully degrades to local limits during Redis cluster outages.
use_cases: API gateway ingress protecting backend microservices from denial-of-service traffic surges
Multi-tenant SaaS tier enforcement (free tier 60 req/min vs enterprise tier 5,000 req/min)
Authentication endpoint brute-force protection throttling failed login attempts per client IP
hard_parts: Writing atomic Redis Lua scripts for sliding-window log and token bucket algorithms with zero race conditions
Achieving sub-3 millisecond gateway proxy overhead under heavy multi-tenant request loads
Designing circuit-breaker fallback to localized in-memory token buckets when Redis nodes fail
Accurately computing and propagating HTTP rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, Remaining, Reset)
screener_signals: Clean Go implementation separating reverse proxy, Redis Lua scripts, configuration, and metrics
High-concurrency benchmark demonstrating strict rate enforcement under 20,000 concurrent requests
Anti-fake verification script sending dynamic client bursts across threshold and asserting exact 429 status transitions

components.name: HTTP Reverse Proxy Gateway
components.purpose: Intercepts inbound HTTP requests, extracts tenant API keys or client IPs, and proxies valid traffic

components.name: Atomic Redis Lua Limiter
components.purpose: Executes atomic sliding-window counter and token bucket evaluation inside Redis without race conditions

components.name: Multi-Tenant Quota Matcher
components.purpose: Resolves client identity to tier limits (e.g. Bronze 100/min, Gold 5000/min) from dynamic configuration

components.name: Circuit Breaker Fallback Engine
components.purpose: Detects Redis health degradation and switches to local in-memory token buckets to keep proxy operational

architecture.data_flow: Inbound HTTP requests arrive at the Go reverse proxy; the Quota Matcher identifies client identity and rate quota rules; the proxy executes an atomic Lua script in Redis passing client key and time window; Redis calculates remaining capacity and updates sliding window counters atomically; if within quota, the proxy forwards the request to upstream backends with rate limit headers; if exceeded, the proxy terminates the request with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; if Redis is unresponsive, the Circuit Breaker diverts evaluation to local in-memory buckets.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: HTTP 429 status code returns with RFC 6585 Retry-After headers; Redis Lua script atomicity preventing concurrent race exploits.

targets.method: Proxy round-trip latency overhead benchmark excluding upstream backend execution duration
targets.input: 50,000 requests processed through rate limiter proxy to mock zero-latency upstream server
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+, local Redis 7 instance over Unix socket or TCP
targets.minimum_pass: p99 proxy overhead latency is < 3.0 milliseconds
targets.target: p99 proxy overhead latency is < 1.2 milliseconds
targets.report: Latency benchmark summary output reporting p50, p95, and p99 percentiles

targets.method: Bursted traffic test sending 1,000 requests against a configured limit of 500 requests per minute
targets.input: 1,000 concurrent HTTP requests dispatched by 20 worker threads within a 5-second window
targets.minimum_pass: Gateway permits exactly 500 requests and rejects exactly 500 requests with HTTP 429
targets.target: Gateway permits exactly 500 requests and rejects exactly 500 requests with HTTP 429
targets.report: Traffic enforcement verification log reporting HTTP status code counts

targets.method: Automated SIGSTOP/kill chaos injection against Redis during active proxy request stream
targets.input: 5,000 continuous requests during simulated Redis downtime event
targets.minimum_pass: Gateway fails over to local in-memory limiting within 100ms with 0 unhandled 500 errors
targets.target: Gateway fails over to local in-memory limiting within 100ms with 0 unhandled 500 errors
targets.report: Chaos resilience log detailing circuit breaker state transition and request error rates

rubric.evidence_location: Terminal test summary log and reports/status_distribution.json
rubric.pass_criterion: Exactly 500 HTTP 200 and 500 HTTP 429 responses recorded with exit code 0

rubric.input: Redis process termination during active 5,000 request stream
rubric.expected_result: Circuit breaker trips to local in-memory token bucket; proxy returns 0 HTTP 500 errors

rubric.expected_result: Response contains HTTP 429 status and X-RateLimit-Limit, Remaining, and Retry-After headers

rubric.expected_result: Gateway allows first 10 requests and transitions to HTTP 429 on exactly the 11th request

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a distributed Go reverse proxy rate limiting gateway using Redis Lua scripts, multi-tenant tiers, and circuit breaker fallback.
worksheet.q2: Target users: API platform engineers, backend infrastructure engineers, and systems architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: API gateway ingress protection, multi-tenant tier quota enforcement, and login endpoint brute-force throttling.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: atomic Redis Lua sliding-window logic, sub-3ms gateway latency overhead, circuit breaker local fallback, and RFC 6585 header handling.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 500 simulated tenant configurations across 3 service tiers. Synthetic mock credentials only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: Miniredis in-memory mock.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Redis network latency overhead. Fallback: connection pooling and pipeline batching.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded 200/429 alternating responses. Anti-fake check 5 configures dynamic key with limit 10 and asserts transition on exactly request 11.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic API keys and simulated HTTP workloads only.
